oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts detected in hosted API (region: us-west-2). Error rate spike started ~5m ago. Paging @sre-oncall.

alex: seeing same. spike from 2% -> ~18% 5xx on /v1/generate. latency distribution tailing. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/2487654322

alex: sample curl failing repeatedly: `curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'` returns `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and `upstream timeout` in gateway logs.

rui: logs show lots of `batcher: queue wait > 1200ms, size=1` and `scheduler: head-of-line blocking detected` in runtime.

alex: stack snippet from runtime: ```
[2026-03-15 09:21:02] WARN batcher: enqueue wait 1350ms cid=abc123 route=prod-usw2
[2026-03-15 09:21:02] ERROR scheduler: dispatch failed: deadline exceeded (kv-cache lock contention?)
```

dawn: I'm oncall and woke up to PD page. joining now. any customer-reported outages?

alex: some customer errors bubbled to CSMs — AcmeCorp and ScribeAI reported 5xx in the last 10m. Not widespread 100% but errors affect subset of requests hitting certain routes.

kyle: hypothesis: surge of small requests caused continuous batching to fill slow slots -> head-of-line tasks stuck waiting for long-running request in same batch -> downstream gateway times out. Also seeing scheduler saturation on a subset of workers.

sophia: can we verify per-worker queue depth? rui do you have `kubectl exec` access to runtime metrics cluster?

rui: pulling metrics now. `sum(rate(batcher_queue_depth[1m]))` shows a spike on pool-gpu-7 and pool-gpu-8. Also `scheduler_active_batches` near capacity on those nodes.

alex: logs show repeated `model-inference: token-gen stall` from model variant `opt-8q`. Might be one model variant degraded.

dawn: mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from affected pools to backup pool; 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for high-latency routes; 3) increase gateway timeout/buffer and throttle non-critical traffic; 4) scale up dedicated pools (if capacity available).

kyle: we can flip the routing policy to prefer `pool-burst` which has spare capacity. I can push that in routing service. Plan to also lower `max_batch_wait_ms` from 1000 -> 50 for the problematic route to avoid HOL. That will increase token cost but reduce tail latency.

sophia: agree, do both. do it in this order: route away -> lower batch wait -> monitor. If that doesn't work, force-evict long-running requests on affected schedulers.

rui: initiating routing change now: `POST /service/routing/update {"route":"/v1/generate","prefer_pools":["pool-burst"],"region":"us-west-2"}` -> 202 Accepted

oncall-bot: ROUTING_CHANGE: route update initiated by rui. ID=route-evac-2487654322.

alex: lowering batch wait on prod route: `rbac run config set batcher.max_batch_wait_ms 50 --route /v1/generate --region us-west-2`

kyle: applied. confirm via metrics. watching `p50/p95/p99` for token latency.

rui: metrics: queue depth on pool-gpu-7 dropping, active_batches dropping from 98% -> 62% in 60s. 5xx rate falling from 18% -> 6% in 2m.

dawn: good. still seeing intermittent 502s from gateway when a worker fails to accept connection. investigating worker health.

alex: noticed OOM restarts on worker nodes around the same time. `kube` shows 3 restarts on node node-7 over last 10m. Could be memory spike from an old quantization path.

kyle: ok, let's cordon node-7 and drain to prevent re-scheduling noisy tasks there. `kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` in progress.

sophia: notify SRE infra to patch driver that caused memory spike. I’ll open an infra ticket.

dawn: customer impact update: AcmeCorp reported ~12 failed requests in last 15m; ScribeAI reported degraded latencies for background jobs. No revenue-critical customer fully down. Estimated impact: 3-7% of total requests in us-west-2 experienced errors or timeouts during peak.

alex: adding temporary rate limit on incidental non-auth traffic to free capacity: `gateway policy add rate-limit --route /embeddings --rate 10rps`

rui: also blacklisting the degraded model variant `opt-8q` for new requests: `model-router disable opt-8q --region us-west-2 --reason "suspected stall"` -> success. New requests now prefer `opt-8` and `opt-8-quant` variants.

kyle: after these changes, error rate stabilized around 1.6% and p99 latency improved ~420ms -> ~190ms on /v1/generate.

sophia: good stabilization. plan next: 1) replace degraded nodes (node-7) ASAP, 2) run node memory profiling to find leak, 3) postmortem draft, 4) evaluate batcher default `max_batch_wait_ms` for this workload.

dawn: taking ownership of oncall for next hour. I'll coordinate with infra for node replacement. handing off to @sophia in 30m.

sophia: taking handoff. key facts: routing evac + batch wait lowered + opt-8q disabled. Current status: stable. I'll keep incremental monitoring and liaise with CSMs.

alex: notes to include in incident writeup: root cause likely HOL blocking due to combination of slow model variant and default batching thresholds + a simultaneous node memory noise that concentrated load. Immediate mitigation: route evac, throttle, lower batch wait, disable model variant, drain noisy node.

rui: saving logs and traces to incident bundle: s3://incidents/2487654322/bundle.tar.gz

dawn: CSM update sent: "We identified transient routing congestion in us-west-2 causing increased latencies and intermittent 5xx on some requests. We've routed traffic away, disabled the problematic model variant, and nodes are being replaced. No extended customer outage expected. Will follow up with timeline + postmortem."

alex: small follow-up: consider adding a proactive HOL detector in the scheduler to auto-lower batch wait for routes that exceed queue-wait thresholds.

kyle: +1. also think about a circuit-breaker that sends a route to backup pool if per-route 5xx > 5% for 2m.
